style: Static locked camera, three-quarter view facing screen-right, matching the reference, the whole body, weapon and shield always inside the frame with a margin, the face visible, the flat solid magenta background never changes. Clean anime game sprite animation, crisp lines. Hair, cloth, cape and loose pieces always keep moving with natural delay and follow-through, never frozen.

segments.name: A
segments.prompt: A chibi young knight with messy brown hair, small golden antlers with green leaves and green eyes, in bronze and gold armour with a white fur collar, a green leaf-pattern tabard and cape, a stone-and-gold war hammer in his right hand and a tall rectangular green tower shield with a golden tree emblem in his left,,, from his guard stance sets himself to charge: he steps his front foot forward, rocks his weight onto his bent back leg, leans in and presses his shoulder against the inside of his tall tower shield, which he swings round to face the foe at chest height, and lets the hammer drop low and trail behind his hip, his head staying clearly visible above the shield rim, into the pose of the last frame. Feet adjust minimally between the supplied endpoint stances, staying grounded without sliding or hopping; no turning or scale change. Arms, shoulders and torso drive the action; hair, cloth and cape follow with natural overlapping motion. Preserve his identity, costume, proportions and the single rigid hammer and the single shield, always drawn whole and clearly visible. No added effects, aura, glow, dust or particles.

pick_note: A s7 từ thế thủ vào thế lấy đà (mốc WINDUP 14/11: vai tì khiên, khiên chĩa về địch, búa kéo thấp sau hông), B s7 bật lao khiên, mốc rush cũ; roles: cast1 và cast2 cùng về thế lấy đà (giữ sống), cast4 lao khiên giữ sống tới cast5
why_size_lock: owner 14/11 ('thu người lại trông không được đẹp'): the rise out of the old crouch drew him ~15% taller for two frames
redo_note: 14/11 (owner: "Nori1. Khi tung tuyệt kỹ có thu người lại trông không được đẹp"): the low crouch hidden behind the shield (Qwen key "crouch") replaced by a tall braced stance, shield planted, hammer over the shoulder (Codex key BRACE, f1_cast_keys.py); clips A, B and the living hold redrawn. Then (owner: "Nori 1 không được. Tôi vẫn muốn là dùng khiên để huých vào địch ... Tôi muốn tư thế lấy đà để cầm khiên lao vào địch"): BRACE (hammer over the shoulder) replaced by WINDUP, the run-up to the shield charge: shoulder in the shield, hammer trailing.
sharpen_note: The stone-and-gold war hammer is ONE whole rigid weapon held in his right hand in every cell, never missing, never melted into a smear: his fist always grips the BOTTOM END of the long straight handle by the golden pommel, the stone head at the other end. Where the soft clip blurs or loses the hammer while he trails it low behind him through the run-up and the shield rush, draw it whole in his hand, between its positions in the neighbouring cells (held low behind his hip, the head trailing near the ground). The tall tower shield stays whole in his left hand. The hammer head is exactly the one in Image 2 in every cell: the same big rectangular grey stone block with gold bands and the golden tree emblem, the same size relative to his head; never smaller, thinner, rounder, bent or stretched, even where the soft clip shrinks or warps it (owner 14/11 circled cells where the clip deformed it). The handle stays straight and the same length and thickness as in Image 2.
why_sharpen_note: owner 14/11 ("Búa lỗi này"): the first BRACE gripped the hammer by its neck; clip B loses the hammer mid-swing

sharpen_sheet_notes.2: In every cell where he lunges behind the shield, the hammer trails behind him at its FULL length: his fist at the bottom end of the long handle by the golden pommel, the whole straight handle visible between his fist and the stone head, as long as in Image 2; never a short handle, never the hand next to the head (Codex round 5). His shoulder drives forward into the shield, the shield pushed ahead at chest height: a forceful shove, not an open stretch.
